data.name: Tommy
data.gender_notes: Tommy is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name ‘Tomas’, meaning ‘twin’. In the Bible, a popular bearer of this name is Thomas, one of the twelve apostles. Thomas is known as ‘Doubting Thomas’ because he doubted Jesus’ resurrection until he saw the wounds and was given permission to touch them. The name Tommy carries the meaning “Twin” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tommy usually hope their child will grow to embody twin and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Tommy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Twin.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tommy total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: טומי
in_hebrew.meaning: מקור השם תומאס, תום, תומי, כפיר אלוקים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם טומי הוא צורה מקוצרת של השם תומאס, שמקורו בארמית ומשמעותו 'תום, תומי, כפיר אלוקים'. השם תומאס היה שמו של אחד מתלמידיו של ישוע, הידוע גם כ'תומאס המאמין'. השם הפך לפופולרי בקרב הנוצרים בגלל הקשר שלו לישוע ולתורתו.

in_greek.name: Τόμι
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Τόμι, σημαίνει πιστός στον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τόμι είναι μια σύντομη μορφή του ονόματος Θωμάς, το οποίο προέρχεται από το αρμενικό και σημαίνει 'δίδυμος'. Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ιωάννη, ο Θωμάς αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού Χριστού. Ο Θωμάς είναι γνωστός ως 'Θωμάς ο πιστός' λόγω της αμφιβολίας του για την ανάσταση του Ιησού και της επακόλουθης επιβεβαίωσης της πίστης του.

in_latin.name: Tommy
in_latin.meaning: Name Tommy means Twin, a devoted one to God
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Tommy is derived from the Latinized form of the Aramaic name Thomas, meaning 'twin'. The name Thomas was popularized by one of Jesus' twelve apostles, known as Thomas the Apostle. Thomas is often referred to as 'Doubting Thomas' due to his initial skepticism about Jesus' resurrection. The name Tommy has been used in Christian tradition as a diminutive form of Thomas, signifying devotion to God and faith.

in_english.name: Tommy
in_english.meaning: Derived from Thomas, meaning twin, a devoted one to God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tommy originates from the Hebrew name 'Taoma', meaning 'twin', and was later adapted into Greek as 'Θωμάς' (Thomas). In Christian tradition, Thomas was one of Jesus' twelve apostles, often referred to as 'Doubting Thomas'. The name Tommy, a diminutive form of Thomas, signifies a person who is devoted to God, strong in faith, and possibly having a dual nature. Throughout history, the name has been popularized in various Christian cultures, symbolizing spiritual devotion and sincerity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Tommy' is primarily found in Western countries, and it has been used as a given name for boys since the Middle Ages. The name gained immense fame in the 19th century when British statesman and politician, Thomas Canning (Lord Palmerston), was born. The name also became popular through the centuries due to various cultural influences such as Thomas Alva Edison, Thomas Mann and Tommy Dorsey, among others.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name 'Tommy' is deeply rooted in the biblical concept of brotherhood and faith. The name ‘Tomas’ (Tommy) signifies 'twin'. This name is a reminder that we all are connected to each other as brothers and sisters in God’s family, and we need to have faith in one another and in His divine plan, even when faced with doubts and uncertainties, as Saint Thomas exemplified.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tommy's name derived from Thomas, an apostle known for his doubt and skepticism towards the resurrection of Jesus. Yet, Thomas' faith was strengthened when he personally encountered the risen Christ, leading him to declare, "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28), a profound declaration of faith and devotion. Thus, Tommy symbolizes the human struggle with doubt and the journey towards unwavering faith and belief in the divine.
